questions.question: A load is 40 feet long. What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed to secure it?
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers and trailers without sides, cargo must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: You feel sleepy while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to finish the trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Leave the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel sleepy, stop driving and get rest. Fighting exhaustion is dangerous and causes many deadly crashes. Energy pills do not help — they wear off and make you more tired than before.

questions.question: How can you prevent fatigue while driving?
questions.explanation: A warm, stuffy cab makes you sleepy. Open a window, use a vent, or turn on the air conditioning to keep the cab cool and reduce fatigue.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what should you do with the glad hands?

options.text: Glad hands can be connected to any other glad hands.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.explanation: Connect only matching glad hands when coupling. They are usually color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, they are acceptable on rear tires.
Yes, they are acceptable when carrying heavy loads.
Yes, they are acceptable in combination vehicles.

questions.explanation: Inspect your wheels before driving. Look for damage on wheels and rims. Do not use wheels or rims that have been welded — they are not safe.

questions.question: What can water collected on a road cause?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, you should check all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: The cargo is heavier at the top than the bottom.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is heavier at the top than the bottom.
questions.explanation: When inspecting cargo, make sure it is balanced and secured properly. Keep the weight as low as possible to prevent rollovers. Do not overload the trailer.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: Which vehicle type is most prone to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to roll over from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: On icy roads, should a retarder be turned on or off?

options.text: Used only on the rear wheels.

questions.explanation: A retarder can cause skids when traction is poor, such as on icy roads. Turn off the retarder in these conditions.

questions.question: When starting a trip with cargo, the driver should:

options.text: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles.
Drive faster than usual to test if the load is secure.
Only use side mirrors to check the cargo.
Not check the cargo again if it was secure before starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo security before the trip starts, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: Mismatched tire sizes:

options.text: Can be used on a tractor.
Can be used on a trailer.
Should be used in bad weather.
Should not be used on any vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used on any vehicle.
questions.explanation: Mismatched tire sizes are a problem that must be fixed if found during a vehicle inspection.

questions.question: When stopping, you should apply the brake pedal by:
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down slowly when stopping. Slow braking helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: An emergency brake must be controlled by:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency and parking brakes. Use mechanical force because air pressure can leak away over time.

questions.question: If a vehicle's ABS stops working while driving, the driver should:

options.text: Use the parking brake to stop.

questions.explanation: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) fails, the vehicle's basic brakes still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: Rolling backward when starting to accelerate is dangerous because:

options.text: The truck is not designed to go backward.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Make sure you can accelerate without rolling back first. Rolling backward can cause you to crash into a vehicle or object behind your truck.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Stop cargo from being loaded too high.
Stop cargo from being unloaded too quickly.

questions.explanation: Blocking is placed in front, behind, or on the sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle moves.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:

options.text: Pressed down quickly with both feet.

questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down slowly to stop the vehicle smoothly and safely.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Protect the driver from cargo hitting them.
Protect the driver's head when getting into the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo hitting them.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver from cargo that shifts forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: Alcohol starts to affect the body:
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms muscle control, reaction time, sight, judgment, and decision-making. For some people, even one drink causes impairment. Do not drive any vehicle after drinking any amount of alcohol.
